assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
a knowledge graph of canonical entities and a typed-tag taxonomy (PLACE/TOPIC/PERSON/ORG/EVENT) are available
a semantic-relatedness index (ESA or an IC-bearing taxonomy) and a co-occurrence corpus are available
the geo/topic relevance rule is editorially specified and revisable from feedback
exclusions: building the knowledge graph and tag taxonomy themselves (delegated upstream)
downstream rendering, publishing, and serving of accepted scenes
training the ESA/relatedness model from raw corpora
audience-segmentation modeling beyond the homophily/shareability prior (delegated to niche__audience_segmentation)
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for entity-linking and geo-relevance combination work units, informed by record-linkage theory, semantic-relatedness models, knowledge-graph entity linking, homophily, and link-prediction; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Fellegi & Sunter 1969 A Theory for Record Linkage (JASA); Resnik 1995 Using Information Content to Evaluate Semantic Similarity (IJCAI); Gabrilovich & Markovitch 2007 Computing Semantic Relatedness using Wikipedia-based Explicit Semantic Analysis (IJCAI); Shen, Wang & Han 2015 Entity Linking with a Knowledge Base (IEEE TKDE) and Hoffart et al. 2011 Robust Disambiguation of Named Entities (AIDA, EMNLP); McPherson, Smith-Lovin & Cook 2001 Birds of a Feather: Homophily in Social Networks (Annual Review of Sociology); Adamic & Adar 2003 Friends and Neighbors on the Web (Social Networks)

competency_questions.question: How is each surface mention resolved to one canonical entity id and disambiguated to the right KB node?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTITY_RESOLUTION canonicalizes and dedups; MENTION_DISAMBIGUATION links to the correct KB sense

competency_questions.question: How does the typed-tag join keep PLACE:punjab distinct from TOPIC:punjab?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TYPED_TAG_JOIN uses a (type,value) join key so cross-type label collisions never join

competency_questions.question: What closed set of relation types is assigned to each edge and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RELATION_TYPING assigns SAME_PLACE/SAME_TOPIC/AFFECTS/CONTRASTS_WITH from a closed set

competency_questions.question: Which relations are symmetric and which are directional, and how is direction stored?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYMMETRY_DIRECTIONALITY classifies AFFECTS as directed and the SAME_*/CONTRASTS as symmetric

competency_questions.question: How is relatedness between two entities computed from semantic and co-occurrence evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RELATEDNESS_SCORE blends ESA/IC semantic relatedness with COOCCURRENCE_SIGNAL and a LINK_PREDICTION_PRIOR

competency_questions.question: What structural and audience priors inform link plausibility and shareability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LINK_PREDICTION_PRIOR gives an Adamic-Adar topology prior; HOMOPHILY estimates audience-overlap shareability

competency_questions.question: How does the geo-relevance predicate license a link rather than relatedness alone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GEO_RELEVANCE_PREDICATE gates relatedness into a geo/topic-conditioned relevance license; HOMOPHILY feeds shareability

competency_questions.question: How are topically-tempting but irrelevant joins rejected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPURIOUS_LINK_GUARD vetoes high-relatedness pairs that fail the relevance predicate

competency_questions.question: How is each licensed link weighted by its shared high-weight tags?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LINK_STRENGTH aggregates shared high-IDF tags and relatedness into an edge weight

competency_questions.question: How does generation produce many candidates while ranking keeps the precise top?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CANDIDATE_GEN_VS_RANK separates high-recall blocking from precise top-k ranking by LINK_STRENGTH

competency_questions.question: How is the hard arity-2-to-3 constraint enforced on a scene?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARITY_2_3 rejects singletons and arity>3 and selects the strongest 2-3 mutually relevant nodes

competency_questions.question: How is mutual/pairwise relevance closure verified within a 3-node scene?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MUTUAL_RELEVANCE checks triad closure (closed vs hub-and-spoke) under ARITY_2_3

competency_questions.question: How are relatedness/relevance thresholds calibrated and corrected by human feedback?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION selects the PR operating point and routes possible-matches to review; FEEDBACK_RELABEL recalibrates guards, thresholds, and the relevance rule from editorial labels

competency_questions.question: How is per-link confidence/provenance captured and the assembled scene validated end-to-end against its invariants?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_PROVENANCE attaches confidence and an evidence trace; SCENE_VALIDATION gates arity-2-3, relevance-licensed edges, guard-clear, closure, direction, and provenance with a per-check reason

glossary.definition: the single normalized id an entity resolves to after alias and transliteration dedup
a (type,value) pair (e.g. PLACE:punjab) used as a join key so type namespaces never collide
a symmetric [0,1] magnitude of semantic + co-occurrence association between two entities
the boolean geo/topic-conditioned rule that LICENSES a link, distinct from relatedness
a licensed, validated group of exactly 2 or 3 mutually relevant entities
the count of nodes in a scene; constrained to the closed interval {2,3}
the principle that similar nodes associate, used to estimate audience overlap and shareability
a topically-tempting pair that is highly related yet fails the relevance predicate
the Fellegi-Sunter log-likelihood-ratio score thresholded into match/possible/non-match zones
the property that all three pairs in a 3-node scene are mutually relevant (vs hub-and-spoke)

nodes.definition: Resolve every surface mention to one canonical entity id and merge aliases/variants (spellings, transliterations, role titles) so that downstream joins compare entities, not strings. Implements probabilistic record linkage: a match weight is the log-likelihood ratio of agreement on each field given match vs non-match, thresholded into match / possible-match / non-match zones.

base.update_signal: blocking key, comparison vector, or match/non-match thresholds change

pros.claim: A single canonical id per entity makes joins and relatedness compare real entities instead of raw strings, killing duplicate-driven errors
pros.example: merging 'Bhagat Singh', 'Shaheed Bhagat Singh' and the Punjabi transliteration onto one id

cons.claim: Over-merging collapses two genuinely distinct entities into one and is hard to reverse downstream
cons.example: merging two different people who share a common name into one canonical id

failure_modes: over-merge of distinct entities (false-match zone too wide)
under-merge leaving aliases as separate ids (blocking key too strict)
acceptance_tests: each surface mention maps to exactly one canonical id and no two canonical ids share a known alias set
revisit_triggers: duplicate canonical ids observed in production joins

nodes.definition: Disambiguate an ambiguous surface mention to the correct knowledge-graph node using local context and global coherence (collective linking), so 'Punjab' the Indian state, 'Punjab' the Pakistani province, and 'Punjab' a band each link to distinct nodes. Combines a prior commonness probability with context similarity and entity-coherence, as in AIDA-style collective disambiguation.

base.update_signal: candidate-generation source or coherence model changes

pros.claim: Collective disambiguation using inter-entity coherence resolves mentions a per-mention prior alone gets wrong
pros.example: co-occurring 'Amritsar' pushes ambiguous 'Punjab' toward the Indian-state node

cons.claim: Coherence optimization is expensive and can propagate one wrong anchor into several linked errors
cons.example: a mis-linked seed entity drags coherent neighbors to the wrong sense

failure_modes: popularity prior overrides correct rare sense
context window too small to disambiguate homographs
acceptance_tests: a held-out mention set links to the gold KB node above the target accuracy threshold
revisit_triggers: disambiguation accuracy regresses on the audit set

nodes.definition: Join entities and news items on TYPED tags, where a tag is a (type, value) pair so that PLACE:punjab is never joined to TOPIC:punjab or ORG:punjab. The type namespace (PLACE / TOPIC / PERSON / ORG / EVENT) is the join key alongside the value, preventing the classic label-collision error where a place name and a topic name share a string.

base.update_signal: tag type namespace or join-key definition changes

pros.claim: Typing the join key eliminates the most common spurious link: a place string colliding with an unrelated topic or org string
pros.example: PLACE:punjab vs TOPIC:punjab kept distinct so a wheat-farming topic does not auto-link to a Punjabi musician

cons.claim: A rigid type namespace rejects legitimate cross-type bridges that a richer relation model would keep
cons.example: a PLACE and the EVENT named after it are not joinable on bare typed tags

failure_modes: untyped join silently links place to topic on a shared string
type vocabulary too coarse to separate ORG from EVENT
acceptance_tests: no join exists between two tags that share a value but differ in type
revisit_triggers: a cross-type collision link is observed downstream

nodes.definition: Assign each candidate link a relation type from a closed set: SAME_PLACE, SAME_TOPIC, AFFECTS, CONTRASTS_WITH. The relation type carries the semantics the scene exposes and determines which downstream checks (e.g. directionality for AFFECTS) apply. Relation typing turns an undifferentiated 'related' edge into an interpretable, checkable claim.

base.update_signal: the closed relation-type set is revised

pros.claim: A closed, typed relation set makes each edge an interpretable claim and lets type-specific rules (directionality, contrast) be enforced
pros.example: tagging a Punjab-person <-> US-India-immigration edge AFFECTS rather than a vague 'related'

cons.claim: A closed relation set forces edges that are genuinely a blend into one bucket, losing nuance
cons.example: an edge that is both SAME_TOPIC and CONTRASTS_WITH must pick one

failure_modes: relation type left null so directionality cannot be checked
forcing a blended relation into a single wrong type
acceptance_tests: every emitted edge carries exactly one relation type from the closed set
revisit_triggers: an edge's assigned type contradicts its directionality check

nodes.definition: Compute a relatedness score between two entities combining (a) distributional/semantic relatedness — Explicit Semantic Analysis cosine over concept vectors, or IC-based similarity over a taxonomy — with (b) empirical co-occurrence in a corpus. Relatedness is the continuous magnitude that ranks candidate links; it is symmetric and bounded to [0,1].

base.update_signal: relatedness model (ESA index, taxonomy, or co-occurrence corpus) changes

pros.claim: Blending distributional relatedness (ESA) with corpus co-occurrence captures both meaning-level and usage-level association, beating either alone
pros.example: ESA relates 'diaspora' and 'immigration' even without surface co-occurrence; co-occurrence catches a fresh news pairing ESA misses

cons.claim: Semantic relatedness is not relevance: two entities can be highly related yet irrelevant to license together
cons.example: 'cricket' and 'India' are very related but that relatedness alone does not justify a news scene

failure_modes: high relatedness mistaken for a license to link
stale ESA index undervalues an emerging association
acceptance_tests: relatedness is symmetric, in [0,1], and ranks a gold related pair above a gold unrelated pair on the audit set
revisit_triggers: co-occurrence corpus refreshed and rankings shift materially

nodes.definition: Estimate the empirical co-occurrence component of relatedness: how often two entities appear together in the same document/window beyond chance, using pointwise mutual information (PMI) or a normalized variant. Supplies the usage-level evidence that complements model-based semantic relatedness.

base.update_signal: co-occurrence corpus, window size, or PMI normalization changes

pros.claim: Chance-corrected co-occurrence (PMI) surfaces genuine associations and discounts pairs that co-occur only because both are frequent
pros.example: PMI keeps a rare-but-tight pairing while discounting two ubiquitous entities

cons.claim: Raw PMI is unstable for low-frequency pairs and over-rewards rare co-occurrences
cons.example: two entities co-occurring once get an inflated PMI

failure_modes: low-count pairs produce unstable, inflated PMI
window too wide dilutes real co-occurrence with noise
acceptance_tests: PMI estimates are frequency-smoothed and a rare ubiquitous pair scores below a tight rare pair

nodes.definition: Provide a structural link-prediction prior from the existing entity graph: the Adamic-Adar score (sum over shared neighbors weighted by inverse log degree) and common-neighbor counts estimate how plausible a new edge is from graph topology alone, independent of text. Used as a prior that nudges candidate generation and tie-breaks relatedness.

base.update_signal: the underlying entity graph or neighbor-weighting changes

pros.claim: A topology prior (Adamic-Adar) predicts plausible links from shared low-degree neighbors even when text evidence is thin
pros.example: two people sharing a rare-neighbor 'Jallianwala Bagh' get a high structural prior

cons.claim: Structural priors entrench existing graph bias and under-predict genuinely novel cross-community links
cons.example: a first-of-its-kind connection has no shared neighbors and is scored low

failure_modes: sparse graph yields near-zero priors for all new pairs
high-degree hub neighbors inflate spurious priors
acceptance_tests: Adamic-Adar ranks a held-out true edge above a sampled false edge on the link-prediction audit

nodes.definition: Model homophily — the principle that contact and shared interest concentrate among similar nodes ('birds of a feather') — to estimate audience overlap between two entities. High audience overlap makes a link more shareable and engaging; homophily explains why links within an interest community travel further than cross-community links.

base.update_signal: audience-overlap measurement or homophily weighting changes

excluded: the relevance predicate (overlap is not relevance)

pros.claim: Homophily-based audience overlap predicts which true links will actually be shared and engaged with, improving scene value
pros.example: two cricket entities share a fan audience, so their scene spreads within that community

cons.claim: Optimizing for homophily creates filter bubbles and starves valuable cross-community (bridging) links
cons.example: always linking within the diaspora community hides relevant outside-community context

failure_modes: over-weighting homophily collapses scenes into one echo community
audience-overlap proxy stale or biased
acceptance_tests: scenes with high audience overlap show higher measured engagement than low-overlap scenes on the audit cohort
revisit_triggers: bridging-link share rate falls below target

nodes.definition: Define the boolean relevance predicate that LICENSES a link A<->N: license only when relevance(A,N) holds under a geo/topic-conditioned rule, not merely when relatedness is high. Example: a Punjab-rooted person links to a US-India-immigration news item because the geo lineage makes the person relevant to that story; relevance gates relatedness into an actual permission to link.

base.update_signal: the relevance rule, geo-conditioning, or relatedness->relevance gate changes

pros.claim: A relevance predicate separates 'these are related' from 'these may be linked here', which is the difference between a coherent scene and a topical pile
pros.example: Punjab person <-> US-India immigration is licensed by geo lineage, while Punjab person <-> unrelated Punjab band is not

cons.claim: A hand-tuned relevance rule is brittle and can encode a narrow editorial bias as if it were ground truth
cons.example: a geo rule that demands birthplace match rejects a diaspora-relevant link

failure_modes: relevance conflated with relatedness so any related pair is licensed
geo rule too strict, rejecting valid diaspora relevance
acceptance_tests: the predicate licenses a curated set of gold-relevant pairs and rejects a curated set of related-but-irrelevant pairs above target precision/recall
revisit_triggers: a related-but-irrelevant link passes the predicate in audit

nodes.definition: Reject topically-tempting but irrelevant joins: pairs that score high on relatedness or share a string yet fail the relevance predicate. Acts as a hard negative filter against the most seductive false positives (shared rare word, trending co-mention, popularity coincidence) that a relatedness-only ranker would license.

base.update_signal: the spurious-pattern catalog or hard-negative rules change

pros.claim: An explicit guard against tempting false positives raises scene precision far more than tightening the relatedness threshold, which also kills true links
pros.example: vetoing a 'both mention cricket' link that has no real relevance instead of raising the global threshold

cons.claim: An aggressive guard suppresses subtle-but-real links that resemble known spurious patterns
cons.example: a legitimately oblique relevant link is filtered as if it were a popularity coincidence

failure_modes: a trending co-mention is licensed as if relevant
guard over-filters subtle true relevance
acceptance_tests: the guard rejects a curated hard-negative set (string collisions, trend coincidences) while passing curated true links

nodes.definition: Weight each licensed link by the strength of its evidence: the sum/aggregate of shared HIGH-WEIGHT tags (rare, specific, high-IDF tags count more than common ones), combined with the relatedness magnitude. Link strength orders the licensed edges so the scene can keep its strongest links and the workflow can rank scenes.

pros.claim: Weighting by shared rare/specific tags (IDF-style) makes a link backed by a distinctive shared tag outrank one backed by a generic tag
pros.example: a shared PLACE:jallianwala_bagh tag outweighs a shared TOPIC:india tag

cons.claim: IDF-style rare-tag weighting can over-reward a single quirky shared tag and inflate a thin link
cons.example: one rare shared tag pushes a weakly relevant pair to the top

failure_modes: common tags dominate strength because IDF weighting missing
a single rare tag over-inflates a weak link
acceptance_tests: link strength ranks a multi-rare-tag-shared edge above a single-common-tag-shared edge
revisit_triggers: ranking inversions observed against editorial judgment

nodes.definition: Separate candidate generation (cheap, high-recall: produce MANY plausible pairs via blocking, typed-tag overlap, and the link-prediction prior) from ranking (expensive, high-precision: keep the TOP pairs by relatedness, relevance, and link strength). The two-stage design controls the quadratic blow-up of all-pairs comparison while preserving recall.

base.update_signal: blocking strategy or generate-vs-rank split changes

pros.claim: Generate-many-keep-top bounds the O(n^2) pairing cost while keeping recall, the standard record-linkage blocking pattern
pros.example: blocking on shared typed tags reduces comparisons by orders of magnitude before precise scoring

cons.claim: A lossy blocking key drops true pairs that never enter the candidate set, capping achievable recall
cons.example: a true link whose entities share no blocking tag is never generated

failure_modes: blocking key too tight: true pairs never generated
ranking stage starved by a too-permissive generator
acceptance_tests: recall on a gold candidate set stays above target after blocking, and top-k ranking precision meets target
revisit_triggers: recall at generation stage drops below target

nodes.definition: Handle the symmetry/directionality of each relation: SAME_PLACE and SAME_TOPIC are symmetric (A~B iff B~A) while AFFECTS is DIRECTIONAL (A AFFECTS N does not imply N AFFECTS A) and CONTRASTS_WITH is symmetric. Relatedness is symmetric but the relevance and relation layers are not, so the scene must store and render direction where it matters.

pros.claim: Storing AFFECTS as a directed edge preserves the causal/influence reading a symmetric edge would destroy
pros.example: 'immigration policy AFFECTS Punjab family' is not the same claim as the reverse

cons.claim: Tracking direction doubles edge bookkeeping and invites inconsistent direction labels
cons.example: an AFFECTS edge stored with the wrong head/tail flips the claim

failure_modes: a directional AFFECTS edge stored or rendered as symmetric
symmetric relation needlessly duplicated as two directed edges
acceptance_tests: AFFECTS edges are directed and SAME_PLACE/SAME_TOPIC/CONTRASTS_WITH edges are symmetric in storage and rendering

nodes.definition: Enforce the hard arity constraint that a licensed scene links EXACTLY 2 or 3 nodes: reject a singleton (arity 1, nothing to relate) and reject a sprawl (arity > 3, no longer a focused scene). Arity is a checkable obligation evaluated after relevance licensing and link-strength ranking, selecting the strongest 2-3 mutually relevant nodes.

base.update_signal: the arity bounds (2..3) or selection rule change

pros.claim: A hard 2-3 arity bound keeps every scene focused and rejects both empty singletons and unfocused sprawls deterministically
pros.example: a 5-entity pile is trimmed to the 3 most mutually relevant, and a lone entity is rejected as no scene

cons.claim: A rigid 2-3 bound rejects a genuinely coherent 4-entity scene that belongs together
cons.example: a tight quartet must be split or one true member dropped

failure_modes: a singleton or 4+ scene slips through unfiltered
trimming to 3 drops a node more relevant than one kept
acceptance_tests: every licensed scene has arity 2 or 3; singletons and arity>3 are rejected with a reason
revisit_triggers: a >3 or singleton scene reaches output

nodes.definition: Verify mutual (pairwise) relevance closure within a 3-node scene: it is not enough that A-B and A-C are relevant; for a coherent triad the rule decides whether B-C must also be relevant (closed triad) or whether a hub-and-spoke pattern (A central) is acceptable. Prevents incoherent triads where two members are licensed only through a third.

pros.claim: Requiring (or explicitly allowing) triad closure stops scenes whose third member is relevant only via a hub, keeping the triad genuinely coherent
pros.example: rejecting A-B-C where B and C have nothing relevant in common beyond both touching A

cons.claim: Strict closure rejects valid hub-and-spoke scenes where a central entity legitimately bridges two others
cons.example: a person who genuinely connects two otherwise-unrelated events is rejected by closure

failure_modes: an incoherent hub-only triad licensed
valid hub-and-spoke triad rejected by over-strict closure
acceptance_tests: every 3-node scene satisfies the configured closure policy (full closure or declared hub-and-spoke)

nodes.definition: Calibrate the thresholds that turn continuous relatedness and the relevance score into discrete keep/reject decisions: choose the operating point on the precision-recall curve, map Fellegi-Sunter-style match/possible/non-match zones, and route possible-matches to review. Calibration is the dial that trades scene precision against recall.

base.update_signal: operating point, PR target, or review-routing policy changes

pros.claim: An explicit calibrated operating point makes the precision/recall trade auditable instead of an emergent accident of model scores
pros.example: setting the threshold at the PR knee and routing the ambiguous band to human review

cons.claim: A single global threshold is wrong for heterogeneous relation types that need per-type operating points
cons.example: one threshold over-licenses SAME_TOPIC while under-licensing AFFECTS

failure_modes: one global threshold mis-serves a relation type
possible-match band not routed to review
acceptance_tests: the chosen operating point meets the target precision at the required recall on the calibration set
revisit_triggers: precision or recall at the operating point falls below target

nodes.definition: Attach to each licensed link a confidence score and a provenance trace: which typed tags matched, the relatedness and co-occurrence components, the relevance rule fired, and the alternatives rejected. Confidence supports thresholding and downstream trust; provenance supports audit, explanation, and targeted repair of a bad scene.

base.update_signal: confidence definition or provenance schema changes

pros.claim: A provenance trace makes every scene explainable ('why these entities?') and makes repair precise instead of a blind retry
pros.example: answering 'why is this person in the immigration scene' with the matched geo tag and the AFFECTS rule

cons.claim: Full provenance per link adds storage and write overhead proportional to candidate volume
cons.example: logging every rejected alternative for every candidate pair balloons storage

failure_modes: missing provenance prevents targeted repair
confidence uncalibrated so it cannot gate decisions
acceptance_tests: every licensed link carries a confidence and a provenance trace naming the matched tags and the rule fired
revisit_triggers: a scene could not be repaired for lack of provenance

nodes.definition: Close the loop with human/editorial feedback on emitted scenes: confirmed-good and confirmed-spurious links become labeled examples that recalibrate thresholds, expand the spurious-pattern catalog, and correct the relevance rule. Turns one-shot heuristics into a supervised, continuously-improving system.

base.update_signal: feedback ingestion or relabel policy changes

included: threshold and guard recalibration from labels

pros.claim: Feeding confirmed spurious links back into the guard and calibration steadily raises precision without re-engineering the pipeline
pros.example: a recurring trend-coincidence false positive becomes a new hard-negative pattern after one editor rejection

cons.claim: Feedback that over-fits to a few editors' taste can drift the relevance rule away from broad audience relevance
cons.example: chasing one reviewer's rejections narrows the rule to their idiosyncrasy

failure_modes: feedback over-fits to a small reviewer pool
label leakage between calibration and audit sets
acceptance_tests: confirmed-spurious examples measurably reduce the same false-positive class on the next audit
revisit_triggers: feedback volume or reviewer pool changes
feedback-driven drift detected against the holdout

nodes.definition: Validate a fully assembled scene end-to-end before licensing it for use: arity in {2,3}, every edge relevance-licensed (not merely related), spurious guard clear, mutual-relevance closure satisfied, directionality correct, and a confidence/provenance trace present. The final gate that turns a candidate scene into an accepted, publishable artifact.

base.update_signal: the scene-acceptance checklist or gate criteria change

included: arity + relevance + guard + closure + direction + provenance checks

pros.claim: A single end-to-end acceptance gate guarantees every published scene satisfies all invariants, instead of trusting each step in isolation
pros.example: a scene failing only the closure check is rejected with that specific reason

cons.claim: A monolithic final gate can mask which earlier step is systematically failing if it only reports pass/fail
cons.example: a recurring closure failure looks like a gate problem unless per-check reasons are surfaced

failure_modes: a scene violating an invariant passes the gate
gate rejects without an actionable per-check reason
acceptance_tests: only scenes satisfying arity, relevance, guard, closure, direction, and provenance are accepted; each rejection names the failed check

edges.why_related: the co-occurrence component is summed into the blended relatedness score
audience-overlap signal helps the guard distinguish shareable-relevant from merely-trending links
editorial labels recalibrate the relatedness/relevance operating point
confirmed spurious/relevant labels correct the relevance rule itself
generation yields the candidate pairs the relevance predicate then licenses or rejects
closure over a triad must respect each relation's symmetry/direction
provenance traces feed the spurious-pattern catalog the guard maintains

edges.resolution_rule: relevance dominates: never license a link from relatedness magnitude alone; the geo-relevance predicate must hold even when relatedness is maximal
edges.why_related: high relatedness pressures licensing while the relevance predicate may still reject the link
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: treat audience overlap as a shareability prior, not a license: a high-homophily pair still requires the relevance predicate, and bridging (low-homophily) relevant links are kept
edges.why_related: optimizing for audience overlap pulls toward echo-community links that may not be the most relevant
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: generate for recall, filter for precision: the generator stays permissive and the guard plus relevance predicate remove the tempting false positives it admits
edges.why_related: a high-recall generator floods the pipeline with tempting candidates the precision stages must reject
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: satisfy arity first then closure: when a 3-node scene fails closure, drop to the strongest relevant pair (arity 2) rather than admitting an incoherent triad
edges.why_related: the 2-3 arity target can pressure keeping a third node that breaks mutual-relevance closure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: relatedness_vs_relevance
conflict_axes.description: High semantic/co-occurrence relatedness tempts licensing, but only the geo-relevance predicate should license a link; conflating them produces topical piles.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: relevance predicate gates relatedness; relatedness never licenses alone

conflict_axes.name: homophily_vs_bridging
conflict_axes.description: Audience-overlap (homophily) links are shareable but create echo bubbles; bridging links reach new audiences but are less viral.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use homophily as a shareability prior, not a license; preserve relevant bridging links

conflict_axes.name: recall_vs_precision
conflict_axes.description: A permissive generator maximizes recall but floods the ranker with tempting false positives; a strict generator caps achievable recall.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: generate broad, filter hard with guard + relevance predicate

conflict_axes.name: arity_focus_vs_coverage
conflict_axes.description: A hard 2-3 arity keeps scenes focused but can drop a genuinely relevant fourth node; loosening arity sprawls the scene.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep arity hard; if a 4th is truly needed split into two scenes

conflict_axes.name: closed_triad_vs_hub_and_spoke
conflict_axes.description: Requiring full pairwise closure guarantees a coherent triad but rejects valid hub-and-spoke scenes where one entity legitimately bridges two.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: declare the closure policy per scene type; allow hub-and-spoke explicitly

conflict_axes.name: over_merge_vs_under_merge
conflict_axes.description: Wide entity-resolution thresholds merge distinct entities (over-merge); strict thresholds leave aliases unmerged (under-merge), both corrupting joins.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune Fellegi-Sunter zones; route possible-matches to review

conflict_axes.name: typed_strictness_vs_cross_type_bridges
conflict_axes.description: Strict typed-tag joins kill place/topic string collisions but also reject legitimate cross-type relations a richer model would keep.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep typed join strict; express genuine cross-type ties via RELATION_TYPING (AFFECTS)

conflict_axes.name: rare_tag_weight_vs_thin_evidence
conflict_axes.description: IDF-style weighting rewards distinctive shared tags but a single rare shared tag can over-inflate a thin link.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap single-tag contribution; require corroborating relatedness

conflict_axes.name: feedback_fit_vs_overfit
conflict_axes.description: Editorial feedback raises precision but over-fitting to a few reviewers drifts the relevance rule from broad audience relevance.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold out an audit set; regularize feedback against broad cohorts

edge_cases.description: A place name and an unrelated topic share a string and get joined (PLACE:punjab linked to TOPIC:punjab).
edge_cases.trigger: join performed on bare label instead of (type,value)
edge_cases.mitigation: join only on typed (type,value) keys; never match across type namespaces

edge_cases.description: Two highly related entities (e.g. cricket and India) are licensed into a scene despite no real relevance to the news item.
edge_cases.trigger: relatedness magnitude used as a license without the relevance predicate
edge_cases.mitigation: require the geo-relevance predicate to hold; relatedness alone never licenses

edge_cases.description: A trending co-mention spikes co-occurrence and licenses a coincidental, irrelevant link.
edge_cases.mitigation: chance-correct co-occurrence and gate through the relevance predicate and guard

edge_cases.description: A scene of one entity (arity 1) is emitted with nothing to relate.
edge_cases.mitigation: reject arity<2 with a no-scene reason

edge_cases.description: A sprawling 5-entity pile is emitted as a single scene (arity > 3).
edge_cases.mitigation: trim to the strongest 2-3 mutually relevant nodes or split into multiple scenes

edge_cases.description: A 3-node scene is licensed where the third node is relevant only via a hub, so two members have nothing in common.
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the declared closure policy; drop to arity 2 if closure fails

edge_cases.description: Entity resolution over-merges two distinct people sharing a common name into one canonical id.
edge_cases.trigger: match threshold (false-match zone) set too wide
edge_cases.mitigation: narrow the false-match zone; route possible-matches to human review

edge_cases.description: An AFFECTS edge is stored or rendered symmetric, flipping the causal claim.
edge_cases.trigger: directionality not tracked for a directional relation
edge_cases.mitigation: store AFFECTS as a directed head->tail edge and validate direction at the gate

edge_cases.description: A single rare shared tag over-inflates an otherwise thin link to the top of the ranking.
edge_cases.trigger: uncapped IDF weight on one tag
edge_cases.mitigation: cap single-tag contribution and require corroborating relatedness

edge_cases.description: Blocking key is too tight, so a true relevant pair is never generated as a candidate.
edge_cases.trigger: lossy blocking drops a true pair before scoring
edge_cases.mitigation: use multiple complementary blocking keys to keep recall high

edge_cases.description: A licensed scene has no provenance, so a later-found bad link cannot be repaired without rebuilding.
edge_cases.mitigation: record matched tags, score components, rule fired, and rejected alternatives per link

edge_cases.description: Editorial feedback over-fits the relevance rule to a few reviewers' taste, drifting from broad audience relevance.
edge_cases.trigger: feedback applied without a holdout audit set
edge_cases.mitigation: regularize feedback against a held-out broad cohort and monitor drift

workflow.description: Resolve mentions to canonical ids and dedup aliases/transliterations using Fellegi-Sunter match weights.
workflow.gate: each mention maps to one canonical id; no alias-sharing duplicates

workflow.description: Link each ambiguous mention to the correct KB node via context + coherence.
Join entities and news on (type,value) typed tags, rejecting cross-type collisions.
workflow.gate: no join shares a value across differing types

workflow.description: Produce a high-recall candidate set via blocking, typed-tag overlap, and the link-prediction prior.
workflow.gate: candidate recall above target on the gold set

workflow.description: Compute symmetric relatedness blending ESA/IC semantics with chance-corrected co-occurrence.
workflow.gate: relatedness symmetric and in [0,1]; ranks gold pairs correctly

workflow.description: Assign each candidate edge a closed relation type and route per-type checks.
workflow.gate: every edge has one relation type from the closed set

workflow.description: License only pairs where the geo/topic-conditioned relevance predicate holds.
workflow.gate: no link licensed on relatedness alone

workflow.description: Veto tempting-but-irrelevant pairs (string collisions, trend coincidences).
workflow.gate: curated hard negatives rejected; true links retained

workflow.description: Weight each licensed link by shared high-IDF tags and relatedness, then rank.
workflow.gate: multi-rare-tag links rank above single-common-tag links

workflow.description: Select the strongest 2-3 mutually relevant nodes; reject singletons and arity>3.
Verify triad closure (closed or declared hub-and-spoke) and directionality.
workflow.gate: closure policy satisfied; AFFECTS directed correctly

workflow.description: Run the end-to-end acceptance gate (arity, relevance, guard, closure, direction, provenance) and accept or reject with a reason.
workflow.gate: all invariants satisfied; rejection names the failed check

dominance_rules.rule: GEO_RELEVANCE_PREDICATE must hold before any link is licensed; relatedness magnitude never licenses alone
dominance_rules.rationale: relatedness is not relevance; licensing on relatedness produces topical piles
dominance_rules.trigger: a link is about to be licensed on relatedness score alone
dominance_rules.action: block licensing until the relevance predicate holds

dominance_rules.rule: TYPED_TAG_JOIN must use (type,value) keys; bare-label joins are forbidden
dominance_rules.rationale: place/topic string collisions are the most common spurious link
dominance_rules.trigger: a join is attempted on a bare label
dominance_rules.action: reject the join and require a typed key

dominance_rules.rule: ARITY_2_3 must reduce every scene to exactly 2 or 3 nodes before SCENE_VALIDATION
dominance_rules.rationale: singletons have nothing to relate and arity>3 is an unfocused pile
dominance_rules.trigger: a scene with arity 1 or >3 reaches validation
dominance_rules.action: reject or trim to the strongest 2-3 mutually relevant nodes

dominance_rules.rule: SPURIOUS_LINK_GUARD must clear a pair before it counts toward a scene
dominance_rules.rationale: tempting false positives sink precision more than threshold tuning fixes
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-relatedness pair failing relevance enters scene assembly
dominance_rules.action: veto the pair as a hard negative

dominance_rules.rule: ENTITY_RESOLUTION canonical ids must be fixed before any typed-tag join or relatedness scoring
dominance_rules.rationale: joining or scoring raw strings double-counts duplicates and corrupts ranking
dominance_rules.trigger: a join or score runs on unresolved surface mentions

dominance_rules.rule: MUTUAL_RELEVANCE closure policy must be satisfied for every 3-node scene
dominance_rules.rationale: a hub-only triad is incoherent unless hub-and-spoke is explicitly declared
dominance_rules.trigger: a triad fails the declared closure policy
dominance_rules.action: drop to the strongest relevant pair (arity 2)

dominance_rules.rule: SYMMETRY_DIRECTIONALITY must store AFFECTS as directed before SCENE_VALIDATION
dominance_rules.rationale: rendering a directional relation as symmetric flips the claim
dominance_rules.trigger: an AFFECTS edge is stored symmetric
dominance_rules.action: require a head->tail direction and validate it

dominance_rules.rule: THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION must route possible-match band to review, not auto-decide
dominance_rules.rationale: the ambiguous zone is where over/under-merge and false licensing concentrate
dominance_rules.trigger: a possible-match is auto-accepted or auto-rejected

dominance_rules.rule: CONFIDENCE_PROVENANCE must be present on every licensed link before publishing
dominance_rules.rationale: without provenance a bad scene cannot be repaired or explained
dominance_rules.trigger: a link reaches output without a provenance trace
dominance_rules.action: block publishing until provenance is recorded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not license links on relatedness before the relevance predicate exists; relabeling a relatedness-only batch later is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mass un-licensing of topical piles after the relevance rule lands

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not join on bare labels; retrofitting typed keys after collisions requires re-joining everything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full re-join after place/topic string collisions are discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip entity resolution before scoring; deduping after ranking invalidates all scores
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-scoring every pair after duplicate canonical ids are merged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not emit scenes without enforcing arity; trimming sprawls after publishing breaks already-shared scenes
Do not over-merge entities with a wide false-match zone; un-merging a collapsed entity requires reprocessing its links
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cascading link rework after an over-merge is reversed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not store AFFECTS symmetrically; correcting direction after rendering requires re-validating every directional edge
anti_rework_rules.prevents: bulk direction re-validation after a symmetric-storage bug

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip provenance recording; reconstructing why a scene was licensed requires re-running the whole pipeline
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full pipeline replay to debug a single bad scene

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune one global threshold across relation types; per-type recalibration later forces re-deciding every band
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-decision of all borderline links after splitting thresholds per relation type

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply editorial feedback without a holdout; un-drifting an over-fit relevance rule requires reverting and re-auditing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rule rollback and re-audit after feedback-driven drift

iteration_protocol.action: tighten the relevance predicate in GEO_RELEVANCE_PREDICATE and add the pattern to SPURIOUS_LINK_GUARD

iteration_protocol.trigger: a place/topic string collision is observed
iteration_protocol.action: verify the join uses (type,value) keys in TYPED_TAG_JOIN and audit the candidate generator

iteration_protocol.trigger: a scene with arity 1 or >3 reaches validation
iteration_protocol.action: re-run ARITY_2_3 selection and confirm SCENE_VALIDATION rejects out-of-range arity

iteration_protocol.trigger: an incoherent hub-only triad is published
iteration_protocol.action: enforce the closure policy in MUTUAL_RELEVANCE and drop to arity 2 on failure

iteration_protocol.trigger: over-merge or under-merge observed in canonical ids
iteration_protocol.action: re-zone Fellegi-Sunter thresholds in ENTITY_RESOLUTION and route possible-matches via THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION
add complementary blocking keys in CANDIDATE_GEN_VS_RANK and re-check TYPED_TAG_JOIN coverage

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reversed-direction AFFECTS edge is found
iteration_protocol.action: fix directional storage in SYMMETRY_DIRECTIONALITY and re-validate at SCENE_VALIDATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: feedback-driven drift detected against the holdout
iteration_protocol.action: regularize FEEDBACK_RELABEL against the broad cohort and re-audit THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION

priority_rationale: ENTITY_RESOLUTION/MENTION_DISAMBIGUATION/TYPED_TAG_JOIN are foundational; RELATEDNESS_SCORE and GEO_RELEVANCE_PREDICATE are the relatedness-to-relevance core; SPURIOUS_LINK_GUARD and ARITY_2_3 gate scene precision and shape; MUTUAL_RELEVANCE, CONFIDENCE_PROVENANCE and SCENE_VALIDATION close the method last.
